newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Steelmaker Clabecq future in doubt after vote.
newsitem.headline: Steelmaker Clabecq future in doubt after vote.

text.p: The future of bankrupt Belgian steelmaker Forges de Forges de Clabecq SA hung by a thread on Wednesday after workers rejected a pension package and the representative of a firm trying to buy the plant said the vote threatened the deal.
On Tuesday 55.7 percent of the voting workers rejected the pension offer after following the advice of some trades unions that the payments were too low and there was no guarantee for the future.
"It is clear that the workers do not want social peace. They do not want us," Roberto Grosso, the Belgian representative of Swiss-Italian steel and commodity broker Duferco told RTBF radio.
Duferco is the only firm so far identified as being interested in trying to take over the steelworks.
"We have said all along that the price for saving Clabecq was social peace. They evidently don't want it...and must take the consequences," Grosso added.

Aware of the sword hanging over the heads of their members, and in a bid to reverse the result, two unions called on Wednesday for a special poll to be taken of the 200 workers who had for technical reasons been barred from voting.
The plan aimed to alleviate the consequences of bankruptcy for the workers and make the company attractive for a takeover.
There have been clashes between police and the steelworkers since Clabecq, based in the small town of Tubize south of Brussels, was declared bankrupt in January.
The workers are due to meet again on May 15 to discuss future plans.
